title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: many cognitive experiments, want know whether stimulus pattern influences behavior even participants aware . test , researchers often collect two paired measures participants: direct task (asking directly whether noticed masked stimulus statistical regularity) indirect task (measuring behavioral effect, priming faster response times). uSDT package brings paired data together hierarchical Signal Detection Theory (SDT) framework, helping test key hypotheses unconscious processing within single unified model. tutorial, walk three straightforward steps: Prepare data: Use usdt_data_tasks() usdt_data_long() get paired measures ready modeling. Fit model: Run hsdt() fit hierarchical SDT model. model estimates overall task sensitivities, subject-specific sensitivity values, tests three key hypotheses unconscious processing. Inspect results: Visualize key model estimates plot(), quantify reliability group subject-specific levels usdt_reliability(), add parametric bootstrap inference usdt_boot() needed.

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: usdt_data_tasks() combines two tasks single paired dataset. specify subject, condition, response columns, map levels signal noise roles. Whenever argument shared across tasks, can pass single value (like subject_col = "subj"). tasks differ, provide list per task using list(direct = ..., indirect = ...):
code: data_usdt <- usdt_data_tasks(   # One data frame per task   direct   = vadillo_awareness,   indirect = vadillo_cuing,    # Shared subject column   subject_col = "subj",    # Condition mapping (shared column name and labels here)   condition_col    = "condition",   condition_levels = c(signal = "old", noise = "new"),    # Response columns differ: judgements vs continuous response times   response_col = list(direct = "judged.old", indirect = "rt"),    # How responses map to signal vs noise   response_levels = list(     direct   = c(signal = 1, noise = 0),     indirect = c(signal = "faster", noise = "slower")   ),    # Dichotomize continuous response times using a median split   dichotomize = list(direct = FALSE, indirect = TRUE),      # Contrast coding scheme across conditions (deviation by-default)   coding = "deviation" )

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: coding argument affects response criterion (also called “bias parameter”) represents model. Task sensitivity (d') remains identical schemes: "deviation" (default): Codes signal +0.5 noise -0.5. intercept reflects overall response bias centered stimulus distributions. "treatment": Codes noise 0 signal 1. intercept reflects criterion relative baseline (noise) condition. default, uSDT uses deviation coding.

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: Setting dichotomize = list(direct = FALSE, indirect = TRUE) converts continuous RTs binary responses via median split computed within subject across trials, following approach proposed Meyen et al. (2022). case: RTs subject’s median count "faster" (signal responses). "hit" old display searched faster median, "false alarm" new display searched faster median. design, splitting exactly median balances fast slow responses across trials. deviation coding, balance centers indirect decision criterion zero (c \approx 0). , hsdt() fixes indirect criterion zero default whenever mean absolute subject criterion 0.02 (can override fix_criteria = "none").

title: Fitting a hierarchical SDT model
text: summary breaks model two primary structural components presenting hypothesis tests: Fixed effects (group-level means): fixed estimates describe average task performance across participants. , mean sensitivity reliably zero direct task (d' = 0.24, p < .001) indirect task (d' = 0.13, p < .001), indicating -chance recognition significant contextual cuing effect overall. direct criterion (-0.04, p = .215) shows substantial group-level response bias. determined data preparation, indirect criterion fixed zero therefore omitted estimation. Random effects (individual differences): parameters capture -subject variability around group means. standard deviations (sd(d')) reflect individual variability sensitivity tasks. correlation parameter (cor(d') = 0.49) estimates latent association direct indirect sensitivity across participants, though wide confidence interval indicates considerable uncertainty around estimate.

text: make consequences measurement error intuitive, plot() compares standard regression observed sensitivities model’s latent regression side side:  contrast two panels illustrates core problem: Observed estimates (left panel): Regressing raw indirect d' raw direct d' ignores measurement error. Unreliability severely flattens slope (b_1 = 0.043) artificially pushes intercept upward (b_0 = 0.118, p < .001). applied researcher relying standard regression mistakenly conclude compelling evidence unconscious processing d'_{\text{Direct}} = 0. Model-estimated sensitivities (right panel): hierarchical model corrects trial-level noise. Grey segments show shrinkage raw d' model-implied d' values (green points). Accounting unreliability steepens latent slope (b_1 = 0.356) pulls intercept near zero (b_0 = 0.044, p = .701, marked vertical dotted line).

code: meyen_split(x, by, signal = c("faster", "slower"), ties = c("noise", "random"))

title: Dichotomize response times into binary choices — meyen_split
text: x Numeric vector continuous values, typically response times. Vector identifying subject observation x. Medians computed independently participant. signal Character string specifying side median treated "signal" response SDT framework. Use "faster" target condition speeds responses (e.g., facilitatory priming, spatial cueing) "slower" slows responses (e.g., interference, Stroop-like effects). ties handle trials match subject's median exactly. "noise" assigns noise category (0). "random" breaks ties random, keeping cell proportions balanced possible.

title: Dichotomize response times into binary choices — meyen_split
text: integer vector 0s (noise response) 1s (signal response) matching length x. Missing values (NA) preserved.

title: Dichotomize response times into binary choices — meyen_split
text: odd number trials (\(n\)), dataset split two equal halves median falls exactly observed trial. Setting ties = "noise" assigns middle trial noise, producing signal proportion \((n - 1) / (2\cdot n)\) slightly shifting response criterion. practice, difference (\(1 / (2\cdot n)\)) negligible, setting ties = "random" resolves ties probabilistically avoid systematic directional bias.

title: uSDT 0.1.0
text: usdt_data_tasks() usdt_data_long() prepare paired direct indirect measures report column mappings preparation diagnostics. Every column, level format argument takes either one value tasks one per task list(direct = ..., indirect = ...), two tasks may differ columns use, values columns take, format arrive . meyen_split() dichotomizes continuous responses using within-subject median pooled across conditions, following Meyen et al. (2022). sdt_moments() computes subject-level SDT estimates optional sampling variances without fitting hierarchical model.

title: uSDT 0.1.0
text: hsdt() fits binomial probit mixed model correlated random sensitivities returns three hypothesis tests. sensitivity_diff(), latent_cor() latent_regression() calculate mean sensitivity difference, latent correlation latent regression. usdt_tests() collects analytical tests one table. usdt_boot() adds parametric bootstrap inference fitted object’s hypothesis table enough usable replicates available.
